podcast.body: A driving electro rock song with a "stompy electro rock vibe" that Max Martin first applied to Katy Perry's "I Kissed a Girl." On this track, Pink channeled her emotions into bravado, even opening the song with a taunting chant. Despite its punchy sound, "So What" was surprisingly personal, addressing her trial separation from her husband, Carey Hart. Pink, a "great believer in music as therapy," poured her hurt feelings into this defiant song, in which she literally calls herself a "rock star." Released in August 2008, it was an instant smash, debuting at number 9 on the Hot 100 and climbing to number 1 just three weeks later, marking her first entirely solo number one hit and her first trip to the penthouse since the "Lady Marmalade" cover in 2001. "When So What landed in August 2008, it was an instant smash, debuting all the way up at number 9 on the Hot 100 and rising to number 1 just three weeks later."
